prTitle: Add OpenAI SDK Audio Speech support

content.motivation: The code change introduces support for OpenAI Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities within the Spring AI framework using the official OpenAI Java SDK. This enables developers to easily configure and utilize audio speech generation features through standard Spring Boot auto-configuration and property-based settings.
goodPoints: Correct use of @ConfigurationProperties for managing model configuration in a Spring-idiomatic way.
Comprehensive suite of integration and unit tests covering default and custom configurations.
Proper resource management for input streams using try-with-resources to prevent memory leaks.
Clean abstraction of rate limit metadata using HTTP header extraction.
Correct implementation of the AutoConfiguration setup and dependency injection pattern.
badPoints: The code uses a raw RuntimeException when handling IO errors in the model execution.

The logger naming convention triggered a static analysis warning, although it currently follows standard Java conventions; the PMD warning might be a false positive related to the specific ruleset configuration.
Tight coupling between the model implementation and the underlying HTTP client setup logic.
content.suggestion: Define a specific domain exception (e.g., OpenAiSdkAudioException) to wrap checked IOExceptions instead of throwing raw RuntimeException. Additionally, consider decoupling the OpenAI client creation process further by abstracting the client factory logic, though the current builder pattern is acceptable for the project scale.

details: Configures the OpenAI client via OpenAiSdkSetup.
Uses a builder pattern for configuration and client injection.
Handles the conversion of HTTP responses to speech bytes.
Implements a non-streaming approach to meet current SDK limitations.
Parses OpenAI specific rate-limit headers into a standardized format.

issues.title: Use of Raw RuntimeException
issues.detail: The call method in OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel throws a raw RuntimeException when an IOException occurs. This is not ideal for error handling; a more specific custom exception should be used.

issues.title: Potential Naming Convention Violation
issues.detail: Static analysis flagged the logger field name 'logger' as a potential violation of constant naming rules, although this usually pertains to static final variables meant as constants rather than loggers.

interpretation.changeDescription: Introduced support for OpenAI Audio Speech using the official OpenAI Java SDK by adding OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel, OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechOptions, and their corresponding auto-configuration (OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechAutoConfiguration) and property classes. Added necessary metadata handling for rate limits via OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechResponseMetadata and created corresponding integration and unit tests.
interpretation.changeMotivation: The current Spring AI OpenAI implementation relies on direct REST/WebClient calls. The project is migrating towards utilizing the official OpenAI Java SDK for better maintenance, stability, and access to new features. This change provides the necessary infrastructure to use the official SDK for text-to-speech functionality, enabling users to choose between the legacy REST-based implementation and the new SDK-based one via configuration properties.

checklistItems.title: Are all configuration properties correctly managed via the @ConfigurationProperties class instead of hardcoding values or using @Value?

answer.finalAnswer: All configuration properties are correctly managed via the @ConfigurationProperties class instead of hardcoding values.
answer.analysis: The provided code shows that OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechProperties is annotated with @ConfigurationProperties, which is the correct way to manage configuration properties. The class extends AbstractOpenAiSdkOptions and uses @NestedConfigurationProperty to bind nested properties. There is no hardcoded value in the class; all values are derived from configuration. The @ConfigurationProperties annotation ensures properties are managed via external configuration (e.g., application.yml) rather than being embedded in code.

evidence.reason: The class is annotated with @ConfigurationProperties(OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechProperties.CONFIG_PREFIX), which manages configuration properties from external configuration sources instead of hardcoding values.

checklistItems.title: Does the implementation use constructor injection for the OpenAIClient instead of manual construction within the model or builder?

answer.finalAnswer: Yes, the implementation uses constructor injection for the OpenAIClient instead of manual construction within the model.
answer.analysis: The implementation uses OpenAiSdkAutoConfigurationUtil to resolve connection properties and then constructs the OpenAIClient via OpenAiSdkSetup.setupSyncClient. The OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel constructor takes a Builder that includes the OpenAIClient. This indicates the client is injected via configuration rather than manually constructed within the model.

evidence.reason: The OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel bean is created using OpenAiSdkAutoConfigurationUtil.resolveConnectionProperties and then passed to OpenAiSdkSetup.setupSyncClient, which constructs the OpenAIClient. The model's constructor uses this client, indicating client is injected via the configuration properties rather than manually constructed.

The OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel constructor takes a Builder that includes an OpenAIClient. The client is set via the builder's openAiClient method, which is used during model construction. This suggests client is injected rather than constructed inline.

The AutoConfiguration class does not handle exceptions and does not throw checked exceptions. This violates the checklist item which requires avoiding raw RuntimeException types.

The call method in OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel catches IOException and throws a RuntimeException with message 'Failed to read audio speech response'. This is a raw RuntimeException being thrown directly.

checklistItems.title: Does the OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel maintain a clear separation of concerns, ensuring business logic is appropriately decoupled from the HTTP infrastructure?

answer.finalAnswer: The code does not maintain a clear separation of concerns. Business logic (text-to-speech generation) is implemented in OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel, which directly uses the OpenAI SDK's HTTP client, while the HTTP infrastructure (client setup) is embedded within the model. The auto-configuration class only creates the bean, but does not decouple business logic from HTTP infrastructure.
answer.analysis: The provided code shows the OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechAutoConfiguration class that creates a bean for the model, but the actual business logic (text-to-speech generation) is implemented in OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel, which directly uses the OpenAI SDK's HTTP client. There is no clear separation between the model's business logic and the HTTP infrastructure (OpenAI client setup, HTTP calls). The configuration properties are separate, but the model implementation is tightly coupled to HTTP infrastructure.

answer.finalAnswer: Yes, the unit and integration tests cover both default configuration paths and custom property overrides to ensure auto-configuration reliability.
answer.analysis: The provided code includes integration tests that verify auto-configuration behavior under default settings (autoConfigurationEnabled) and under custom property overrides (customPropertiesApplied). These tests explicitly check that the auto-configuration is enabled with default values and disabled with non-matching property values, covering both paths.
